events.title: Alfred the Great dies
events.description: Alfred, king of the Anglo-Saxons, died after a reign spent defending Wessex against the Vikings. His fortified burhs, navy and promotion of learning in English laid foundations for a unified England.
events.html: Alfred, king of the Anglo-Saxons, died after a reign spent defending Wessex against the Vikings. His fortified burhs, navy and promotion of learning in English laid foundations for a unified England.

events.title: The Erie Canal opens
events.description: Governor DeWitt Clinton set off from Buffalo on the newly completed Erie Canal, which linked Lake Erie to the Hudson River over 363 miles. Cheap transport to the Midwest made New York City the nation's leading port.

events.title: The gunfight near the O.K. Corral erupts in Tombstone
events.description: Wyatt, Virgil and Morgan Earp and Doc Holliday shot dead Billy Clanton and Tom and Frank McLaury in about 30 seconds in Tombstone, Arizona. The fight became the Wild West's most famous legend.
events.html: Wyatt, Virgil and Morgan Earp and Doc Holliday shot dead Billy Clanton and Tom and Frank McLaury in about 30 seconds in Tombstone, Arizona. The fight became the Wild West's most famous legend.

events.title: Ngô Đình Diệm proclaims the Republic of Vietnam
events.description: After a heavily rigged referendum deposed the former emperor Bảo Đại, Ngô Đình Diệm proclaimed the Republic of Vietnam in the south. US support for the regime drew America into the Vietnam War.
events.html: After a heavily rigged referendum deposed the former emperor Bảo Đại, Ngô Đình Diệm proclaimed the Republic of Vietnam in the south. US support for the regime drew America into the Vietnam War.

events.title: Russian forces end the Moscow theatre siege with gas
events.description: Special forces pumped an incapacitating chemical into a Moscow theatre where Chechen militants held some 850 hostages. The attackers were killed, but about 130 hostages died, mostly from the gas's effects.
